title: Staged launch lanes with weekend failover and traffic-slicing playbook
creator: Ethan Brooks
description: Define and document a playbook for staggered launch lanes that combine weekday progressive rollouts with dedicated weekend failover windows. The goal is to reduce blast radius for runtime/console/API changes affecting model routing, kernel selection, or batching defaults and to provide clear on-call runbooks for capacity pressure observed during public launches.
objectives: Minimize user-facing regressions during cross-surface launches by phasing traffic into 4 lanes: Canary -> Wave A -> Wave B -> Global
Provide an automated weekend failover lane (read-only or reduced throughput) to protect signed customers while we remediate regressions
Standardize decision gates and telemetry dashboards so PM/Eng/IR can greenlight roll phases within 2 hours
success_metrics: <1% increase in 99th pct latency vs baseline for Waves A/B within first 24h
Rollback rate <= 3% of launches that triggered failover in first 72h
Time-to-decision from first alert to phase halt <= 120 minutes in 90% of incidents
Oncall cognitive load reduction: fewer than 2 ad-hoc playbook escalations per launch
milestones: Align infra and oncall owners + simulate traffic slices (2025-11-28)
First external wave rollout and weekend failover trial (2025-12-19)
rollout_plan: Week 0: Canary (internal + 2% external); Week 1: Wave A (10%), monitor 48h; Week 2: Wave B (40%), monitor 72h; Week 3: Global (100%). Weekend failover window is engaged automatically if sustained SLO breaches or critical errors are observed during weekend maintenance; failover reduces external throughput to 10% and ramps eligible customers to dedicated capacity or queued mode.
canary_criteria: Signal pass on runtime SLOs: latency, error rate, token throughput
No increase in model quality regressions for tracked prompt set (holdout eval) >1%
No critical (>P0) infra alerts acknowledged but unresolved for >30m
Rollout approval recorded in Launch Console with PM and Eng owners listed
communication_plan: Pre-launch: publish playbook link and timeline to #launch-readiness and Launch Console
Day-of: runbook readout with oncall, infra SRE, product ops at 08:30 PT
Phase gates: automated Slack + PagerDuty notifications on threshold breaches
Post-window: mandatory retro in Confluence with timeline, metrics, and decisions
risks: Insufficient observability for multi-tenant traffic-slicing leading to opaque root cause analysis
Weekend failover automation could be too aggressive and block legitimate capacity for paying customers
Coordination overhead across runtime, console, and API owners may slow decision gating
Dependence on ENG-4421 (autoscaling policy hooks) to implement safe throttle behavior
mitigation: Prioritize instrumenting per-tenant latency/cost dashboards before pilot
Clamp automatic failover to 'notify-only' mode for first two weekends; require human confirm for traffic shrink
Designate a single launch owner and deputy with explicit decision authority for each phase
Track ENG-4421 as a blocking dependency and add contingency manual throttle steps if delayed
notes: Trade-offs discussed: more gradual traffic slices reduce risk but increase time-to-value for customers; chosen balance favors safety for runtime-impacting changes
We considered per-customer opt-outs for early waves but will defer until pilot data shows predictable behavior
Weekend failover requires legal/finance review only if we reduce service level for enterprise customers; we flagged for contract team review
